final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor supplied no new admissible evidence and largely reframed the same record more carefully. That clarification is useful, but it does not resolve the core audit concern. The record still shows an exposed named use case, no approved risk acceptance for that exposure, and no evidence that the final launch disclosure is actually present in the launch artifact. This matters because the distinction between a caveated compliant position and a suspicious one turns on whether the caveat describes a completed policy-bounded condition or an unresolved compliance predicate. Here it remains unresolved. A narrower argument against a controls-only theory is more accurate than the original overbroad claim, but accuracy of framing is not evidence that the required condition has been met. Business-cost arguments also do not change the audit outcome.
remaining_concerns: No new admissible evidence was added after the Actor response.
The affected supply-chain vendor screening use case remains exposed in the initial cohort.
The current risk acceptance draft is not approved and does not specifically cover that continued exposure.
No admissible evidence confirms the final launch model card already contains the required disclosure.
The Actor's narrowed rationale is still conditional on a missing compliance predicate rather than proving that predicate is satisfied now.
Under the provided policy text, rollout controls and monitoring are supporting mitigations and do not independently cure an exposed material limitation.
